title: Autodetect embedding norm and runtime adapter for mixed-metric clients
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Problem: Customers are seeing inconsistent reranking results after moving from legacy dot-product clients to newer cosine-normalized embeddings. Some downstream systems still send raw (unnormalized) vectors while newer SDKs normalize before upload. We need a server-side approach that preserves semantics for legacy callers, fixes incorrect score calculations, and avoids large client migrations or breaking changes.

Goal: Ship a runtime adapter that can: (1) autodetect whether incoming embeddings are normalized or raw, (2) apply the correct distance metric (dot vs cosine) or transform (L2-normalize) at scoring time, (3) expose an opt-in header for explicit behavior, and (4) provide a safe, measurable migration path with canarying and a rollback plan.

Constraints: must add minimal per-request latency (target +<0.2ms p50), be compatible with existing caching/batching infrastructure, and not change persisted embedding artifacts or customer-facing storage formats.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime correctly classifies >=99% of incoming embedding batches as "normalized" or "unnormalized" in offline validation
Reranker outputs for legacy clients remain within 1% of historical score ordering when adapter is enabled in compatibility mode
End-to-end p95 latency increase <=10ms in canary traffic and <=0.2ms p50 on steady-state traffic
Feature flag + header controls allow (a) force-dot, (b) force-cosine, (c) auto-detect
Automated tests and integration tests added for classification, normalization transform, and scoring correctness
implementation_summary: We will add a lightweight analyzer stage in the serving runtime that inspects a sampling of vectors in each batch to estimate L2 norm distribution (mean and std). If mean_norm in [0.99,1.01] and std < 0.02 assume normalized. Otherwise assume raw. For raw vectors, options: (A) L2-normalize at scoring time to compute cosine similarity using existing dot-kernel, or (B) compute dot directly if client explicitly requests dot-product via header. The adapter is plumbed as a per-route middleware with a feature-flagged code path and metrics emitted for classification decisions. A per-customer rollout flag will allow gradual enablement. Batching and KV cache keys will include the resolved "embed_mode" (dot|cosine) to avoid cache pollution.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Internal rollout to test tenants — enable auto-detect for 5% of calls with detailed logging. Phase 2: Canary with 1 production customer (opt-in) for 2 weeks, compare rerank AUC and ordering delta. Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with rollback timers. Provide customer-facing opt-out via header 'X-Embed-Mode: dot|cosine|auto' and clear SDK release notes.
rollout_steps: Feature flag hidden: enable on dev/staging clusters
Telemetry: add stats for classify_decision, normalized_ratio, corrections_applied
Canary: 5% random traffic in prod; monitor latency and rerank drift
Customer canary: enable for selected customers with known legacy dot usage
Full rollout: enable by default but honor explicit header and tenant opt-out
tests: Unit: norm estimator edge cases (zero vectors, near-zero std, mixed dims)
Integration: scoring parity harness comparing legacy dot pipeline vs adapter (5000 labeled pairs)
Load: steady throughput 10k req/s ensuring p95 latency targets hold
A/B: evaluate reranker ordering drift and quality metrics (MRR, AUC)
risks_and_mitigations: False classification for mixed-batch inputs: mitigate by sampling strategy + fallback to explicit header when uncertain
Cache fragmentation: include embed_mode in cache key and evict short-lived shards during rollout
Performance regression on long-sequence batches: microbench and add vectorized normalize kernel on hot path
Customer surprise: document behavior, provide header opt-out and SDK patch with explicit flag
comments: 2025-03-11: Spike completed - naive L2 estimator works on sampled vectors; prototype shows 0.001s overhead for 512-d vectors in Go runtime (Riley)
2025-03-14: Design review with API and SDK teams. Agreed to expose 'X-Embed-Mode' header and SDK opt-in helpers (Amara)
2025-03-18: PR #4241 opened with adapter middleware and unit tests. Needs load test results (Eng-Perf)
2025-03-22: Load testing on staging showed p95 +8ms at 5k rps; optimized normalize kernel reduced p95 to +2ms (Amara)
2025-03-25: Canary scheduled next week; creating dashboard and alert runbook for rerank drift >2%
notes: We intentionally avoid changing stored embeddings or adding a new storage format — this keeps customers' persisted artifacts stable.
Consider follow-up to add per-tenant default embed_mode metadata for long-term clarity.
If classification accuracy is insufficient, fall back to conservative behavior: treat as unnormalized and normalize before scoring to preserve cosine semantics.
